gaps.problem: manager is world singleton; markers co mingle
tile hash unpinned; listen host has no net path
gaps.suggestedFix: hash canonical bytes; partition by role

verdict: Mostly correct on 5.6.1-CSS; spine and ReliableMessaging sound but not yet provably bounded.

gaps.problem: Zero-second-copy host has no mod-reachable spatial API: lightweight octree is private; public accessor is a class-keyed TMap; RemoveByInstanceIndex renumbers. Either cache transforms or pay O(N)/cell. Not bounded.
gaps.suggestedFix: Host stores 24-28 B/bldg slim record; read-live only at gather/rebuild; generation-guarded reconciliation after renumbering.

gaps.problem: Strict FIFO at the writer (TQueue Peek/Pop); a big by-value first-join blob blocks later AoI tiles; distance-order only orders the initial enqueue. Bounded O(AoI) join not guaranteed.
gaps.suggestedFix: Cap per-message blob size; keep in-flight window 1-2 messages; app-side priority queue re-sorted by AoI distance; load-test FIFO under join+belt-drag.

gaps.problem: Content-hash version rehashes the full content of every touched tile per change; under belt-drag/blueprint bursts this is residual per-event O(tile-occupancy), hidden by the complexity table.
gaps.suggestedFix: Use a monotonic per-tile uint64 counter bumped O(1) on dirty; hash only lazily off-thread at re-serialize as a client dedupe checksum, not the version identity.

gaps.problem: Workers cannot read live engine arrays (race) and handles are NotThreadSafe, so the game thread must snapshot each changed tile first; server repack is game-thread O(tile-occupancy)/net-tick, not free as implied.
gaps.suggestedFix: Snapshot from the mod own slim columns, coalesced per net-tick; only compression runs on workers; state cost O(sum occupancy of dirty tiles).

gaps.problem: Build.cs has AbstractInstance commented out and ReliableMessaging absent; AbstractInstanceManager has no public collision-disable; GameFeature is LoadingPhase Default with no Shaders dir. Render end-state is new integration, not a flag.
gaps.suggestedFix: Make Slate the default; wire both plugins, confirm linkage on client and dedicated-server, verify a collision-disabled HISM path or build a thin custom marker component.

gaps.area: Anisotropic bounds vs square tile grid
gaps.problem: World is non-square (MAP_WIDTH 750000.66 vs MAP_HEIGHT 750000.00 cm); square WP-aligned tiles and SceneCapture NumXTiles/NumYTiles assume square tiling, yielding ragged edges and per-axis density mismatch.
gaps.suggestedFix: Define the grid in cm with per-axis ceil cell counts; handle ragged edge tiles; set ortho dims per-axis.

gaps.area: Phase C capture isolation + ISM churn
gaps.problem: GetViewOwner/ShowOnlyActors isolation is unverified on the CSS fork (Cartograph_2.0 never compiled); game-thread-only AbstractInstance mutation is unmeasured at 1M.
gaps.suggestedFix: Keep Phase C gated behind Slate until isolation and game-thread mutation budget are proven on a 1M blueprint-stamp burst; if collision can't be disabled, don't use AbstractInstance for markers.

lens: Feasibility on the CSS UE 5.3.2 fork FROM A MOD: are all relied-upon engine features (RDG mod passes, RVT, GPU Scene, Mass, compute rasterization, World Partition server hooks, IFGSaveInterface persistence, ReliableMessaging) actually present and accessible without engine-source edits?

gaps.area: Engine version premise — verified, and it REMOVES most of my lens's teeth (but read the caveat)
gaps.problem: I verified the architecture's central context correction on disk: FactoryGame.uproject EngineAssociation="5.6.1-CSS", NOT 5.3.2 as the prompt assumed. This is decisive and correct — it legitimately removes the 5.3.2 gates the prompt asked me to hunt for (native ortho SceneCapture, current AbstractInstance custom data, UE::Tasks, GPU Scene auto-instancing all ship in 5.6). HOWEVER the architecture then over-claims: it treats '5.6.1' as proof that every upstream-UE-5.6 API is PRESENT AND PUBLIC in CSS's *fork*. CSS forks the renderer heavily (RainRendering plugin, custom FGRenderTargetStage, AbstractInstance replacing stock ISM). A fork can rename, make private, #if-out, or behavior-change any field. Version number != API surface.
gaps.suggestedFix: Re-tag every engine-API dependency not as '5.6 therefore present' but as 'present IFF reachable from a public/binary-exported symbol on the shipped CSS build'. There is NO Engine/ source in this repo (only Source/FactoryGame + targets + Plugins/ — I confirmed no Engine/ dir), so EVERY engine-internal API must be validated against the actual shipped DLL exports / public headers in the SML SDK, not against upstream UE 5.6 docs. Add a one-time 'symbol reachability' spike before any phase that touches a non-FactoryGame engine API.

gaps.area: Phase C — bEnableOrthographicTiling / NumXTiles / NumYTiles (the SceneCapture TDR bound) is UNVERIFIABLE and likely unreachable from a mod
gaps.problem: The architecture's Phase C end-state leans on 'native bEnableOrthographicTiling + NumXTiles/NumYTiles' as a *second engine-native TDR bound* and a load-bearing reason to prefer the GPU capture path. I grepped the entire repo (Source + Plugins + uassets-excluded): bEnableOrthographicTiling, NumXTiles, OrthographicTiling appear in ZERO C++ files. There is no Engine source to confirm the field exists on the fork's USceneCaptureComponent2D, and these fields are config/editor-set UPROPERTYs whose runtime behavior on a forked renderer is unproven. Worse, the open-questions already flag that GetViewOwner/ShowOnlyActors capture isolation 'never compiled' in the Cartograph_2.0 POC — meaning the *prerequisite* for Phase C is historically broken on this exact fork.
gaps.suggestedFix: Already correctly GATED (Phase C is opt-in, with the Slate path as permanent fallback) — so this is not architecture-breaking. But the architecture must STOP citing ortho-tiling as a 'structural TDR bound' in the NET/complexity claims, because it is unverified and may not exist. Demote it to: 'IF the field exists AND honors NumXTiles at runtime on the CSS fork'. The real, verified TDR bound is Phase A's per-tile separate-command-buffer EndDraw, which I confirmed is reachable via the public UKismetRenderingLibrary::Begin/EndDrawCanvasToRenderTarget the mod already calls. Treat Phase A as the only *guaranteed* TDR fix; C is upside.

gaps.area: AbstractInstance hard-depends on AkAudio (Wwise) — enabling it (Phase 4) pulls a heavyweight audio plugin into the mod's build/runtime
gaps.problem: The architecture says enabling AbstractInstance in Cartograph.Build.cs is a simple uncomment. I read AbstractInstance.Build.cs: it lists "AkAudio" in PrivateDependencyModuleNames, and AbstractInstance.uplugin requires the "Wwise" plugin enabled. The manager (AbstractInstanceManager.h) embeds a UAudioGeometryInstanceManager and AddAkGeometryComponent in the core add path. So a visual-only marker layer drags in Wwise/AkAudio coupling — extra link surface, extra init, and a dependency the Cartograph mod's Build.cs currently has AkAudio COMMENTED OUT (//"AkAudio"). This is a concrete build-coupling the design omits.
gaps.suggestedFix: Before Phase 4, confirm AbstractInstance can be linked with AkAudio as a transitive-only dep (the mod itself need not call Ak APIs) and that constructing the manager with no Ak geometry data is a no-op. If Wwise coupling proves problematic, the architecture's own fallback (hand-rolled instance buffer) applies — but note that fallback re-introduces the manual StructuredBuffer patching the design explicitly rejected, so quantify the trade. This reinforces keeping Phase 4 GATED, not default.

gaps.area: ReliableMessaging is a CSS-INTERNAL plugin with a fixed tag enum and no public mod-wiring path — the design assumes more turnkey access than exists
gaps.problem: The architecture treats UReliableMessagingPlayerComponent::SendTaggedMessage as a ready transport the mod just calls. Two disk-verified frictions: (1) FGReliableMessagingTags declares a FIXED enum of FACTORYGAME_API gameplay tags (LightweightSubsystem, MapManager, ConveyorChainSubsystem, ...) — these are CSS's own consumers; a mod-defined tag is fine for SendTaggedMessage's FGameplayTag param, but the design's 'fixed gameplay-tag set' must be mod-registered tags, not these. (2) I found NO code in the repo that attaches UReliableMessagingPlayerComponent to a PlayerController, calls SetTransportLayerConnection, selects the transport-layer factory, or drives the Server_AdvertiseNewConnection handshake — that wiring is CSS-internal/binary. The component is UCLASS(Within=PlayerController) and GetFromPlayer() implies the GAME already attaches it; the mod likely must reuse the game's existing component instance and its already-established transport, NOT stand up its own. If the game only attaches it conditionally (e.g. only when its own subsystems need it), the mod's transport may not exist on a given connection.
gaps.suggestedFix: Spike FIRST: on a live dedicated-server connection, call UReliableMessagingPlayerComponent::GetFromPlayer(PC) and verify (a) a component exists, (b) its transport reports Connected without the mod doing handshake work, and (c) the mod can RegisterTaggedMessageHandler for a mod-owned tag without colliding with CSS's tag dispatch. If the component is NOT auto-attached, determine whether a GameFeature mod can AddComponent + drive the Server_Advertise handshake (the RPCs are protected UFUNCTIONs — a subclass or the game's own flow is needed). This is the single biggest 'secretly needs the game's cooperation' risk in the whole networking story and Phase 0 depends on it entirely.

gaps.area: World Partition server-side cell load/unload events from a mod are UNVERIFIED — the 'O(1) chunk-load via 1:1 WP-cell tiles' claim has no confirmed event source
gaps.problem: serverClientPartitioning hard-couples tile size to WP cell granularity for O(1) chunk-load, and dataFlow's chunk-load flow assumes the client observes 'entering a new WP-aligned region'. I found no WP streaming-source / cell-shown / cell-hidden hook used anywhere in Source/FactoryGame that a mod could subscribe to, and the architecture's own open-questions admit 'whether a mod can observe cell load/unload events on the CSS fork is unverified'. The prompt explicitly flags 'World Partition server hooks' as a suspect feature. WP cell granularity is also an engine/project setting the mod cannot change, so a 1:1 tile==cell coupling is brittle if the cell size differs from the design's ~256 m assumption.
gaps.suggestedFix: DECOUPLE the tile grid from WP cells. The architecture already (correctly, elsewhere) states 'the map-UI viewport AoI is NOT the world-streaming AoI' — so make tiles a mod-owned fixed grid over the constexpr bounds (WEST/EAST/NORTH/SOUTH, which I verified are present) sized independently of WP. Drive tile pulls purely off the map-UI viewport rect, never off WP cell events. This removes the dependency on an unverified WP server hook entirely and makes 'O(1) chunk-load' a non-requirement (there is no chunk-load step if tiles are mod-owned). Keep WP only as a read-only position source for prioritization, which needs no event hook.

gaps.area: FInstanceOwnerHandlePtr is game-thread-only (verified), which caps Phase 4 throughput — but the design's worker-thread story for Phases A/B is sound
gaps.problem: I confirmed on disk: InstanceData.h line 300 — using FInstanceOwnerHandlePtr = TSharedPtr<FInstanceOwnershipHandle, ESPMode::NotThreadSafe>, and the handle inherits TSharedFromThis<...,NotThreadSafe>. So the architecture's claim is correct and it correctly forbids worker-thread handle mutation. The residual gap: in Phase 4, a 1M-building mass-paste or load must perform 1M game-thread SetInstanceFromDataStatic/RemoveInstance calls (each O(1) but each touching a NotThreadSafe TSharedPtr + AddInstanceHandle into a TMap + MarkDirtyDeferred), and these CANNOT be parallelized. The frame-budgeted compositor amortizes this, but a cold first-paint of a megabase becomes a many-frame game-thread drain with NO worker offload available for the handle ops — slower convergence than the design's 'O(1) per-event' framing implies at bulk scale.
gaps.suggestedFix: The design already mitigates correctly (MarkDirtyDeferred batching, frame budget, GATED behind validation). Add an explicit acceptance gate to open-question #2/#3: benchmark game-thread-only handle-write throughput on a 1M cold load and confirm it drains within an acceptable number of frames under the FrameBudgetFraction. If it does not, the verified-safe fallback is to keep Phases A/B (FCanvas/Slate) which DO allow worker-thread POD packing (UE::Tasks on immutable snapshots — feasible, no handle involved), and never promote to C. This is a throughput nuance, not a correctness break.

gaps.area: ReliableMessaging payload-by-value + strict-FIFO + handler-by-rvalue-ref: design correctly adapts, but one detail (in-flight RAM amplification) is under-budgeted
gaps.problem: I verified ReliableMessagingPlayerComponent.h: SendTaggedMessage(FGameplayTag, TArray<uint8> InPayload) IS by-value (architecture correct), the handler is FOnBulkDataReplicationPayloadReceived(FGameplayTag, TArray<uint8>&&) (move, slightly better than the design's by-value claim), and the protocol uses SizeType=int32 + MessageIdType=uint64 (int16-overflow gone, confirmed). PayloadsPendingConnection buffers FULL payloads in RAM until Connected. So a first-join AoI burst materializes: the packed blob + the by-value send copy + the pending-connection queue copy + the chunker's WriteBuffer — up to ~3-4x the AoI bytes resident transiently on the server per joiner during handshake. The design sizes the window for bandwidth but not for this handshake-time RAM multiplier across concurrent joiners.
gaps.suggestedFix: Cap the per-joiner in-flight AoI to a small ring (e.g. enqueue tiles in distance order but only N-deep, refilling on ack) so PayloadsPendingConnection + send copies stay bounded regardless of total AoI size. Confirm the handshake completes (component reports Connected) BEFORE enqueuing the bulk manifest, so PayloadsPendingConnection is not used as the primary buffer. The shared TSharedRef<const> per-tile snapshot already keeps the SOURCE single-copy; just bound the per-connection materialization on top of it.

gaps.area: Slate SLeafWidget + FSlateDrawElement::MakeCustomVerts (Phase B, the 'preferred default') is plausibly reachable but UNCONFIRMED on this fork, and it is now the PERMANENT fallback if C fails
gaps.problem: Phase B is the architecture's preferred 2D end-state AND the permanent fallback when Phase C's capture isolation fails (per open-questions). Its feasibility therefore matters a lot. Slate/SlateCore/UMG ARE in the mod's Build.cs (verified) and MakeCustomVerts is upstream-public, so this is LOWER risk than C — but I found zero usage of MakeCustomVerts/SLeafWidget anywhere in Source/FactoryGame to PROVE the symbol is exported on the CSS Slate build, and the design's '~10x cheaper, ~0 persistent VRAM' Froyok numbers are from a different render context (not a mod compositing into a UMG map panel through the game's HUD). The cross-mod FCanvas::GetBatchedElements hook it removes is real (I confirmed SUBSCRIBE_METHOD(FCanvas::GetBatchedElements ...) at module.cpp:322 with the static_cast hazard at :353), so the motivation is valid.
gaps.suggestedFix: Validate Phase B as a small standalone spike (one SLeafWidget drawing 100k custom-vert quads into the map UMG panel) BEFORE treating it as the default — because it is the fallback when C is blocked, a failure here would leave only Phase A (FCanvas-to-RT, which keeps the 64-96 MB persistent target and the process-wide canvas hook). If MakeCustomVerts composites correctly through FG's UMG/HUD, adopt as default. If not, Phase A remains the floor — still ships the spine + TDR fix, just without the VRAM-to-zero and hook-removal wins. Make this dependency explicit in the phase ordering: A is the guaranteed floor; B's wins are contingent.

gaps.area: Persistent render target preserve-across-EndDraw (Phase A's correctness hinge) is fork-behavior-dependent and historically broke on this code
gaps.problem: Phase A's TDR fix REQUIRES that the 2nd+ BeginDrawCanvasToRenderTarget on the persistent UCanvasRenderTarget2D does NOT implicitly clear/re-init, and that bAutoGenerateMips=false is honored so EndDraw doesn't kick a full-texture mip pass that defeats the scissor. I confirmed the mod uses UKismetRenderingLibrary::Begin/EndDrawCanvasToRenderTarget (public, reachable) and ClearRenderTarget2D. But the architecture's own open-questions cite the branch-history 'lines going crazy' note tracing to exactly this implicit-reclear behavior — i.e. this preserve semantic ALREADY misbehaved on this fork once. If the CSS RHI implicitly clears on BeginDraw, the entire per-tile incremental scheme silently produces a black-except-last-tile map.
gaps.suggestedFix: This is correctly listed as an open question; elevate it to a Phase-2 BLOCKING acceptance test: draw tile A, EndDraw, draw tile B, EndDraw, then read back and assert tile A's pixels survived. If BeginDraw implicitly clears on the CSS fork, the fallback is to bypass UKismetRenderingLibrary and issue the clear+draw via a direct RHI/RDG AddPass with an explicit ERenderTargetLoadAction::ELoad (load, not clear) on the scissored rect — which needs RHI module access (the mod already lists "RHI" in PrivateDependencyModuleNames, verified, so this is reachable WITHOUT engine-source edits). Document ELoad-via-RHI as the concrete Phase-A fallback so a preserve-failure doesn't strand the whole render plan.

gaps.area: Phase N hand-rolled RDG/global-shader rasterizer is correctly rejected — confirmed infeasible as a clean mod on this layout
gaps.problem: Not a gap in the design (it REJECTS this path), but worth affirming under my lens since the prompt explicitly asks about 'RDG mod passes' and 'compute rasterization': the architecture's rejection is CORRECT and well-grounded. I confirmed the Cartograph GameFeature is LoadingPhase=Default (uplugin) with no Shaders/ directory, and there is no Engine/ source to expose renderer-private headers. Shipping global shaders from a GameFeature needs a PostConfigInit shader module + virtual shader path mapping, and RDG passes that do real rasterization touch renderer-private types not exported on a binary fork. So custom-shader rasterization is the one technique that genuinely 'secretly needs engine internals' — and the design already demotes it to optional/profiled-only.
gaps.suggestedFix: Keep it rejected. The only refinement: the design should NOT promise Phase N as a guaranteed escape hatch if Phases A-C cannot hold frame time, because Phase N's feasibility on a binary CSS fork is itself unproven (renderer-private RDG resource types). If A-C are insufficient on an extreme megabase, the honest fallback is aggressive LOD/instance-count culling within Phase B (cull to viewport + zoom-decimate), not a custom rasterizer. State that explicitly so the roadmap has no phantom final tier.

verdict: FEASIBLE AS A MOD ON THE ACTUAL FORK, with the architecture's own gating already covering the worst risks — but the prompt's 5.3.2 premise is wrong and that changes the answer. I verified on disk that the engine is 5.6.1-CSS (FactoryGame.uproject), NOT 5.3.2, which legitimately removes the bulk of the 'needs-newer-UE' feasibility objections my lens was tasked to hunt. The three pillars the design rests on are all present and reachable WITHOUT engine-source edits: AbstractInstance (verified handles + custom-data API, but pulls AkAudio/Wwise), ReliableMessaging (verified int32 sizes / uint64 ids — the int16-overflow crash #9 IS gone by construction — and ReliableMessagingTCP has no Server TargetDenyList so it links on the dedicated server, covering the #9 join path), and UE5Coro (vendored in the mod). The SHARED SPINE (stable generational handles + SoA store + uniform grid + Z-band index + never-cancelled compositor) needs ZERO special engine features — it is pure mod-side data-structure work over the verified constexpr bounds and the verified SML SUBSCRIBE_UOBJECT_METHOD_AFTER hooks on AddBuildable/RemoveBuildable — and is correctly sequenced FIRST. So the spine and Phase A (the guaranteed TDR fix via public UKismetRenderingLibrary Begin/EndDrawCanvasToRenderTarget, already in the codebase) are HIGH-CONFIDENCE buildable today.\n\nThe REAL feasibility exposure is concentrated, not pervasive, and the design mostly gates it correctly. CRITICAL CAVEAT my lens surfaces: there is NO Engine/ source in this repo (only Source/FactoryGame + targets + Plugins/), so every engine-internal API is validated against upstream-UE-5.6 docs, not against the shipped CSS binary's actual exports — 'version 5.6' is being used as a proxy for 'API present and public', which a forked renderer does not guarantee. The two highest-leverage UNVERIFIED dependencies are: (1) [HIGH] ReliableMessaging's player component has no mod-wiring path visible in the repo — it is CSS-internal and the mod almost certainly must reuse the game's already-attached component and established transport rather than stand up its own; if the game doesn't auto-attach it on every connection, Phase 0's entire networking story stalls. This needs a connection-time spike before anything else. (2) [MEDIUM] Phase C's bEnableOrthographicTiling/NumXTiles and GetViewOwner/ShowOnlyActors capture isolation are nowhere in the repo and the POC that tried exactly this 'never compiled' on this fork — but Phase C is already GATED with the Slate path as permanent fallback, so this caps upside rather than breaking the design. Secondary mediums (decouple tiles from unverified WP cell-event hooks; validate persistent-RT preserve-across-EndDraw which historically broke here, with an RHI ELoad fallback reachable since 'RHI' is already a mod dependency; validate MakeCustomVerts compositing through FG's UMG before making Phase B the default since it doubles as the Phase-C fallback) are all addressable mod-side without engine edits. Net: ship the spine + Phase A on high confidence; treat the ReliableMessaging wiring spike as the gating de-risk for Phase 0; keep C/N gated. The architecture does NOT secretly require engine-source changes for any of its committed (non-gated) phases.
